report:
Fresh source review of the complete dependencies claim and all current associations. The three aspects are default availability of the real standard library, availability of its dependency metadata, and the V1 qualification excluding arbitrary third-party dependency configuration. All four implementation associations are ordinary: sage_host::driver, sage_host::metadata, sage_test_harness::compile, and sage_test_harness::compile::rustc. There are no TODO/N/A implementation or test entries.

CompileTest::prepare materializes a standalone normal library package with no Cargo dependencies, uses the production SageHost, and separately invokes rustc. driver::build_rustc_args supplies the pinned sysroot to the normal library metadata stub. Driver::after_expansion retains a live TyCtxt for the request service, and the host installs the corresponding request channel in the database. metadata::our_sysroot supplies SAGE_SYSROOT, whose build-time derivation from rustc --print=sysroot is captured separately in build.rs. The dependency loader deliberately skips building the selected package when direct dependencies are empty because std metadata comes from the sysroot. The current rustc::check now factors execution and output validation into helpers; inspection shows that the invocation still selects our_rustc and passes our_sysroot explicitly, and both helpers propagate failures. Thus this refactoring retains the independent compiler's real standard-library environment. The fixture API provides no third-party configuration fields and prevents replacing Cargo.toml; the scope qualification is respected, not misrepresented as implemented third-party support.

The complete associated test set is one ordinary test, real_std. Its visible fixture declares a std::string::String function parameter and requires diagnostics to equal the empty string. This tests actual standard-library path resolution, including the String re-export backed by dependency metadata, without a fake local standard library. Captured observation code calls function.sig for each function and incorporates accumulated signature diagnostics, so the assertion is meaningful for this parameter. CompileTest::run only reaches the diagnostic comparison after both Sage and independent rustc preparation succeed. The test is adequate for the narrow default-environment claim; arbitrary external dependency fixtures are outside the claim. No new gap or behavioral violation was found. This assessment uses fresh start inputs and captured build.rs and observe.rs context, not the prior recorded verdict. No Rust source or assertions changed in this refresh. No tests were executed by this reviewer during this refresh: the coordinator owns current suite execution, and this report does not carry forward an earlier test run as fresh execution evidence.
